answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
answerStage.answerDesign: 정답 인용: "an attachment that is shown in his artwork." 오류 변형: shown -> showing. 이유: 선행사 an attachment는 artwork에서 '보여지는' 대상이므로 수동태(is shown)가 적절하다. showing으로 쓰면 목적어가 없고 수동 의미가 안 되어 비문이 된다. 반증 검사: 현재 분사로 읽어도 타동사 show의 목적어가 없어 성립하지 않음.

answer.surroundingText: This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that is shown in his artwork.

answerStage.explanation: 주격 관계대명사 that이 이끄는 절에서 선행사인 an attachment(애착)는 그의 예술 작품 속에서 '보여지는' 수동의 대상입니다. 따라서 수동태인 is shown이 되어야 문맥상, 통사상 올바릅니다. showing을 쓰면 진행/능동의 의미가 되어 타동사 show의 목적어가 필요하게 되므로 어법상 틀립니다.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Allan Houser created contemporary Apache sculpture. As a child, he listened to his father's stories about the adventures of Chief Geronimo.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that is shown in his artwork.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: During World War II, he traveled to California, where he became interested in the media of sculpture. He created works in a variety of styles.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: He drew inspiration from both past and present, but like all successful artists, his sculpture transcends race and language.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it can be appreciated by anyone, regardless of his or her background.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 문장의 주어 Allan Houser의 과거 행동을 서술하므로 과거 시제 동사 created를 사용하는 것이 어법상 옳습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 비동사와 결합하여 주어 he의 상태를 나타내며, 관심을 갖게 된 수동적 감정을 표현하므로 과거분사 interested가 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 주어가 단수 명사구인 his sculpture이므로, 수일치 규칙에 맞게 단수 동사 형태인 transcends를 쓰는 것이 옳습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 문맥상 조각품(it)은 감상되는 수동적 대상이므로 조동사 뒤에 수동태인 can be appreciated를 쓰는 것이 옳습니다.

question.explanation: 주격 관계대명사 that이 이끄는 절의 선행사는 an attachment입니다. 애착(attachment)은 예술 작품 속에서 보여지는(수동) 대상입니다. showing은 뒤에 목적어를 취해야 하는 능동 형태이므로 목적어 없이 전치사구 in his artwork만 이어지는 이 자리에서는 비문입니다. 따라서 showing을 수동태를 구성하는 과거분사 shown으로 고쳐야 합니다.
keyPoints: (B) 분사능수동 - 관계절과 선행사의 능동/수동 관계 판단
(A) 정동사/준동사 - 문장 내 정동사 확인
(D) 수일치 - 주어 단복수에 따른 형태 결정
question.passageWithMarkers: Allan Houser __(A) created__ contemporary Apache sculpture. As a child, he listened to his father's stories about the adventures of Chief Geronimo. This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that is __(B) showing__ in his artwork. Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, where he worked as a freelance artist. During World War II, he traveled to California, where he became __(C) interested__ in the media of sculpture. He created works in a variety of styles and mastered bronze, metal, and stone sculpture. Houser's designs are modern, yet firmly rooted in the special tradition of his Native American forefathers. He drew inspiration from both past and present, but like all successful artists, his sculpture __(D) transcends__ race and language. The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it __(E) can be appreciated__ by anyone, regardless of his or her background.

passageText: Allan Houser created contemporary Apache sculpture. As a child, he listened to his father's stories about the adventures of Chief Geronimo. This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that is shown in his artwork. Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, where he worked as a freelance artist. During World War II, he traveled to California, where he became interested in the media of sculpture. He created works in a variety of styles and mastered bronze, metal, and stone sculpture. Houser's designs are modern, yet firmly rooted in the special tradition of his Native American forefathers. He drew inspiration from both past and present, but like all successful artists, his sculpture transcends race and language. The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it can be appreciated by anyone, regardless of his or her background.

answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
answerStage.answerDesign: 정답 자리: 'immersed' (원래 'someone else similarly immersed'). 오류 변형: 'immersing'. 'see' 뒤의 목적어 'someone else'와 2형식/5형식적 관계를 맺고 있는 분사형 목적격 보어 또는 후치 수식분사 자리입니다. 다른 누군가가 '몰입된' 상태이므로 수동/과거분사가 적절합니다. 'immersing'으로 바꾸면 '다른 누군가가 몰입시키고 있는' 능동의 의미가 되어 목적어 부재 등 논리적/구조적 모순이 발생하여 명백한 비문이 됩니다.

answer.surroundingText: Next time you look up, you'll see someone else similarly immersed, and you won't feel alone at all.

answerStage.explanation: 밑줄 친 immersing은 앞의 someone else를 수식하거나 목적격 보어로 쓰이는 분사 자리입니다. '다른 누군가가 책 따위에 몰입된' 상태를 나타내야 하므로, 수동의 의미를 지니는 과거분사 immersed를 써야 올바릅니다. immersing을 사용하면 누군가를 몰입시킨다는 능동 의미가 되어 맥락에 어긋나고 의미를 완성할 목적어도 없으므로 어법상 틀립니다.

question.passageWithMarkers: We all enjoy the pleasure of __(A) being left__ alone with a good book. But sometimes after several hours of immersion we lift our heads and look around, suddenly struck by the quiet, the absence of others. In this situation, we are suffering from reading-induced loneliness. The solution is to read in the company of other people __(B) who__ are reading - whether in a public space such as a café or a library, or in your own home, with your reading friend or partner at the other end of the sofa. Next time you look up, you'll see someone else similarly __(C) immersing__, and you won't __(D) feel alone at all__. Reading can be sociable. Consider joining a reading group __(E) in which__ everybody takes turns reading aloud from a novel. Reading a book collaboratively is a wonderful way to share an otherwise internal and solitary experience.

passageText: We all enjoy the pleasure of being left alone with a good book. But sometimes after several hours of immersion we lift our heads and look around, suddenly struck by the quiet, the absence of others. In this situation, we are suffering from reading-induced loneliness. The solution is to read in the company of other people who are reading - whether in a public space such as a café or a library, or in your own home, with your reading friend or partner at the other end of the sofa. Next time you look up, you'll see someone else similarly immersed, and you won't feel alone at all. Reading can be sociable. Consider joining a reading group in which everybody takes turns reading aloud from a novel. Reading a book collaboratively is a wonderful way to share an otherwise internal and solitary experience.

answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
answerStage.answerDesign: 정답 자리: qualify. 원문 'If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX qualifies as a technology(the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English(Hamlet) must qualify as well.'에서 주어 'a thousand lines'에 맞춰 단수 취급하여 'qualifies'를 썼던 앞선 절 구조에 병렬되어 맥락상 'a thousand lines of letters in English'도 앞과 유사하게 'qualify' 해야 한다는 조동사 must 뒤의 동사원형 자리이다. 만약 이를 qualifying으로 변형하면 조동사 must 뒤에 정동사 없이 준동사만 남아 비문이 된다.

answer.surroundingText: If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX qualifies as a technology (the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English (Hamlet) must qualify as well.

answerStage.explanation: 밑줄 친 부분은 조동사 must 뒤에 오는 동사원형 자리입니다. 주어 'a thousand lines of letters in English (Hamlet)'에 연결되어 주절을 완결하는 정동사(조동사+동사원형)가 필요하므로, 준동사인 qualifying이 오면 비문이 됩니다. 따라서 qualifying을 동사원형인 qualify로 고쳐야 합니다.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX qualifies as a technology (the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English (Hamlet) must qualify as well.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 동사 tend의 목적어 역할을 하는 to 부정사 명사적 용법으로 올바르게 쓰였습니다.

question.explanation: 이 문장의 구조상 조동사 must 뒤에 이어지는 부분은 본동사의 역할을 해야 합니다. 조동사 뒤에는 동사원형이 와야 하므로, 현재분사 형태인 'qualifying'은 문법적으로 불완전하며 정동사 역할을 할 수 없습니다. 따라서 'qualifying'을 동사원형인 'qualify'로 고쳐 기술로서의 자격을 갖춘다는 의미를 바르게 전달해야 합니다.
keyPoints: (C) 정동사 자리 — 조동사 뒤 동사원형
(B) 수일치 — 의미상 하나의 단위 취급

question.passageWithMarkers: We tend to think of technology as shiny tools and gadgets. Even if we acknowledge that technology can exist in disembodied form, such as software, we tend not __(A) to include__ in this category paintings, literature, music, dance, poetry, and the arts in general. But we should. If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX __(B) qualifies__ as a technology (the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English (Hamlet) must __(C) qualifying__ as well. They both can change our behavior, alter the course of events, or enable future inventions. A Shakespeare sonnet and a Schubert symphony, then, are in the same category as Google's search engine and the smartphone: They are something useful __(D) produced__ by a mind. We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies __(E) responsible__ for a Lord of the Rings movie. The literary rendering of the original novel is as much an invention as the digital rendering of its fantastical creatures. Both are useful works of the human imagination. Both influence audiences powerfully. Both are technological.

passageText: We tend to think of technology as shiny tools and gadgets. Even if we acknowledge that technology can exist in disembodied form, such as software, we tend not to include in this category paintings, literature, music, dance, poetry, and the arts in general. But we should. If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX qualifies as a technology (the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English (Hamlet) must qualify as well. They both can change our behavior, alter the course of events, or enable future inventions. A Shakespeare sonnet and a Schubert symphony, then, are in the same category as Google's search engine and the smartphone: They are something useful produced by a mind. We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies responsible for a Lord of the Rings movie. The literary rendering of the original novel is as much an invention as the digital rendering of its fantastical creatures. Both are useful works of the human imagination. Both influence audiences powerfully. Both are technological.

answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

(수동의 의미 또는 형용사화된 분사)

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The human brain is wired to look for threats - a trait that kept us alive when we were living on the savannas but that can prevent happiness in our modern lives.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: This so-called "negativity bias" can keep you focusing on what's going wrong (which explains why complaining is such a popular pastime).

markedExpressions.label: (C)

markedExpressions.label: (D)

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The more you appreciate life, the more reasons you have to celebrate it.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 주어인 The human brain이 자연적으로 그러한 경향이 있도록 만들어진(설정된) 것이므로 수동태 is wired는 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): what은 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사로, write down의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끌며 그 절 내에서 주어 역할을 하므로 어법상 옳습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 전치사 by의 목적어로 쓰인 동명사이므로, sharing의 형태가 올바르게 사용되었습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 'The + 비교급, the + 비교급' 구문으로, '더 ~할수록 더 ~하다'는 의미를 올바르게 형성하므로 The more는 적절합니다.

question.explanation: 이 문장은 5형식 동사 keep(정동사) 뒤에 목적어 you, 목적격 보어가 오는 구조입니다. 동사 keep의 목적어인 you와 보어의 논리적 관계는 수동입니다(네가 외부에 의해 어떤 상태로 집중하게 머무를 때). 따라서 현재분사 형태인 focusing은 비문입니다. 목적어 you가 '집중된' 상태를 유지한다는 의미이므로 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 focused로 고쳐야 합니다.
keyPoints: (B) 목적격 보어의 형태 판단 — 목적어와 보어의 수동 관계 확인
(A) 능동태와 수동태의 구별
(D) 전치사의 목적어로 쓰인 동명사 판단
question.passageWithMarkers: The human brain __(A) is wired__ to look for threats - a trait that kept us alive when we were living on the savannas but that can prevent happiness in our modern lives. This so-called "negativity bias" can keep you __(B) focusing__ on what's going wrong (which explains why complaining is such a popular pastime). To break out of this neural rut, train yourself to acknowledge when things go right. If you keep a calendar or a journal, make a point to write down __(C) what__ went well. If you're more of a verbal processor, start your conversations with friends by __(D) sharing__ a recent win (anything that gives you that yesssss feeling). Where the mind goes, reality follows. __(E) The more__ you appreciate life, the more reasons you have to celebrate it.

passageText: The human brain is wired to look for threats - a trait that kept us alive when we were living on the savannas but that can prevent happiness in our modern lives. This so-called "negativity bias" can keep you focused on what's going wrong (which explains why complaining is such a popular pastime). To break out of this neural rut, train yourself to acknowledge when things go right. If you keep a calendar or a journal, make a point to write down what went well. If you're more of a verbal processor, start your conversations with friends by sharing a recent win (anything that gives you that yesssss feeling). Where the mind goes, reality follows. The more you appreciate life, the more reasons you have to celebrate it.

answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

passageText: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.

answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 스케줄(schedules)이 꽉 채워졌다는 수동적 의미를 지니므로, 명사를 앞쪽에서 수식하는 과거분사 'packed'의 사용은 어법상 적절합니다.

question.explanation: 정답 문장의 골격을 분석해보면, 후반부에 'can improve'라는 명확한 주절의 정동사가 이미 존재합니다. 따라서 문장의 주어 자리에는 명사 역할을 할 수 있는 구문이 와야 합니다. 밑줄 친 자리에 동사원형 'Incorporate'를 사용하게 되면, 문장이 명령문 구조를 취하게 되어 뒤에 이어지는 정동사와 문장 구조상 충돌하는 비문이 됩니다. 따라서 이를 문장의 진짜 주어 역할을 할 수 있도록 동명사 형태인 'Incorporating'으로 고쳐야 어법상 완전히 올바릅니다. 많은 학생이 문두의 동사만 보고 즉시 명령문으로 착각할 수 있지만 구조 전체를 보는 시각이 필수적입니다.

(B) 관계대명사 vs 관계부사 — 완전한 절을 이끄는 부사 where의 쓰임 판단

question.passageWithMarkers: For many of us, making time for exercise is a continuing challenge. Between work commitments and family obligations, it often feels like there's no room in our __(A) packed__ schedules for a dedicated workout. But what if the workout came to you, right in the midst of your daily routine? That's __(B) where__ the beauty of integrating mini-exercises into household chores comes into play. But rather than viewing chores as purely __(D) obligatory__ activities, why not seize these moments as opportunities for physical activity? For instance, practice squats or engage in some wall push-ups as you wait for your morning kettle to boil. __(E) Incorporate__ quick exercises into your daily chores can improve your health.

passageText: For many of us, making time for exercise is a continuing challenge. Between work commitments and family obligations, it often feels like there's no room in our packed schedules for a dedicated workout. But what if the workout came to you, right in the midst of your daily routine? That's where the beauty of integrating mini-exercises into household chores comes into play. Let's be realistic; chores are inevitable. Whether it's washing dishes or taking out the trash, these tasks are an essential part of daily life. answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

question.passageWithMarkers: We have all had the experience of suddenly noticing that a source of constant background noise, __(A) such as__ a distant jackhammer or music from a store, has just ceased - yet we hadn't noticed the sound while it was ongoing. Your auditory areas were __(B) predicting__ its continuation, moment after moment, and as long as the noise didn't change you paid it no attention. __(C) By ceasing__, it violated your prediction and attracted your attention. passageText: We have all had the experience of suddenly noticing that a source of constant background noise, such as a distant jackhammer or music from a store, has just ceased - yet we hadn't noticed the sound while it was ongoing. Your auditory areas were predicting its continuation, moment after moment, and as long as the noise didn't change you paid it no attention. By ceasing, it violated your prediction and attracted your attention. Here's a historical example. Right after New York City stopped running elevated trains, people called the police in the middle of the night claiming that something woke them up. They tended to call around the time the trains used to run past their apartments.

answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 사역동사 have의 목적보어 자리로, 목적어(us)와 목적보어(piling)의 관계가 능동이므로 현재분사를 사용한 것은 적절하다.

question.passageWithMarkers: The fast pace of today's lifestyle has us __(A) piling__ one thing on top of another. But you should know that multitasking doesn't save any time. Focus on one task at a time, and you'll accomplish each task __(E) better__, and probably faster.

passageText: The fast pace of today's lifestyle has us piling one thing on top of another. But you should know that multitasking doesn't save any time. Very often, multitasking only slows you down, contrary to popular belief. Give your whole focus to what you're doing at the moment no matter what it is. While doing the laundry, just do the laundry: Listen to the sound of the water as it fills the washing machine and feel the clothes in your hand. It doesn't take up any more time than it would when done with your phone pressed to your ear. The same applies to your work. Focus on one task at a time, and you'll accomplish each task better, and probably faster.

answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
answerStage.answerDesign: 정답 문장은 'They are often found strolling in large groups toward the edge of the water in search of food.'입니다. 'strolling'은 목적격 보어 혹은 주격 보어(수동태 후)로 쓰이는 현재분사입니다. 이를 정동사 'stroll'로 바꾸면 'are often found stroll'이 되어 비문이 됩니다. 수동태 'are found' 뒤에 동사 원형이 곧바로 올 수 없으므로 명백한 오류입니다.

answer.surroundingText: They are often found strolling in large groups toward the edge of the water in search of food.

answerStage.explanation: 문장의 본동사로 이미 'are (often found)'가 존재하므로, 그 뒤에 또 다른 정동사 'stroll'이 올 수 없습니다. 앞의 'are found'에 이어져 수동태 구문의 주격 보어 역할을 할 수 있도록 현재분사 'strolling'으로 고쳐야 어법상 올바릅니다.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: There is a critical factor that determines whether your choice will influence that of others: the visible consequences of the choice.

markedExpressions.label: (C)

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 'that'은 앞의 명사구 'a critical factor'를 선행사로 받는 주격 관계대명사로, 뒤에 'determines'라는 동사가 이어지는 어법상 올바른 구조입니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 'the leopard seal'을 선행사로 하는 'which'절에서, 주어가 단수이므로 동사 'likes'는 수일치 측면에서 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 'gives up'과 'jumps in'은 'one of them'을 공유하는 병렬 구조로, 주어와 동사의 수일치가 모두 바르게 설정되어 있습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 주어인 'One penguin's destiny'가 3인칭 단수이므로, 뒤따르는 동사 'alters'는 수일치 규칙에 맞게 3인칭 단수형으로 올바르게 쓰였습니다.

question.explanation: 이 문장의 골격은 주어 'They', 정동사 'are often found'로 구성된 수동태 구조입니다. 문장 내에 정동사가 이미 존재하며, 명사 'They'의 상태를 능동적으로 보충 설명하는 주격 보어 자리이므로 밑줄 친 동사원형 'stroll'을 사용하면 정동사가 중복되어 비문이 됩니다. 따라서 'stroll'을 능동 진행의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사 'strolling'으로 고쳐야 합니다. 'find + 목적어 + v-ing' 구조가 수동태로 전환된 형태임을 정확히 파악해야 합니다.
keyPoints: (B) 정·준동사 — 능동의 주격보어 역할을 하는 분사구문 파악
(C) 수일치 — 주격 관계대명사절 내 선행사와 동사의 수일치
(E) 수일치 — 단수 주어 'One penguin's destiny'에 따른 단수 동사

Take the case of the Adélie penguins. They are often found __(B) stroll__ in large groups toward the edge of the water in search of food. Yet danger awaits in the icy-cold water. There is the leopard seal, for one, which __(C) likes__ to have penguins for a meal. What is an Adélie to do? The penguins' solution is to play the waiting game. One penguin's destiny __(E) alters__ the fate of all the others. Their strategy, you could say, is "learn and live."

passageText: There is a critical factor that determines whether your choice will influence that of others: the visible consequences of the choice. Take the case of the Adélie penguins. They are often found strolling in large groups toward the edge of the water in search of food. Yet danger awaits in the icy-cold water. There is the leopard seal, for one, which likes to have penguins for a meal. What is an Adélie to do? The penguins' solution is to play the waiting game. They wait and wait and wait by the edge of the water until one of them gives up and jumps in. The moment that occurs, the rest of the penguins watch with anticipation to see what happens next. If the pioneer survives, everyone else will follow suit. If it perishes, they'll turn away. One penguin's destiny alters the fate of all the others. Their strategy, you could say, is "learn and live."

answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
answerStage.answerDesign: 정답 자리: 'hoping'. 원형 hoping을 hoped로 변형하여 분사구문 능동/수동 문제 출제. 'we'가 'one small effort will erase...'라고 바라는 주체이므로 능동인 현재분사가 필요하다. hoped로 쓰면 수동/과거분사가 되거나 문장에 본동사가 중복되는 비문이 된다.

answer.surroundingText: We call people we haven't spoken to in ages, hoping that one small effort will erase the months and years of distance we've created.

answerStage.explanation: 문장의 본동사는 'call'이고 접속사 없이 컴마 뒤에 이어지므로 분사구문이 자리해야 합니다. 주절의 주어인 'We(우리)'가 뒤의 that절 내용('one small effort will erase...')을 '바라는' 능동의 의미이므로 과거분사나 동사의 과거형인 hoped 대신 현재분사 hoping을 써야 합니다.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We tend to go long periods of time without reaching out to the people we know.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Then, we suddenly take notice of the distance that has formed and we scramble to make repairs.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We call people we haven't spoken to in ages, hoping that one small effort will erase the months and years of distance we've created.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: However, this rarely works: relationships aren't kept up with big one-time fixes. They're kept up with regular maintenance, like a car.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: This isn't to say that you shouldn't bother calling someone just because it's been a while since you've spoken; just that it's more ideal not to let yourself fall out of touch.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 전치사 'without' 뒤에 동명사 'reaching'이 목적어로 잘 쓰였습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 주격 관계대명사 'that'이 선행사 'the distance'를 수식하며 뒤에 'has formed'라는 동사가 이어지는 알맞은 구조입니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 주어 'relationships'가 유지되는 대상이므로 수동태 'are kept up'을 사용하는 것이 문맥상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 조동사 'shouldn't' 뒤에 동사원형 'bother'가 왔으며, '~하는 데 신경 쓰지 말아야 한다'는 의미로 바르게 쓰였습니다.

question.explanation: 정답인 (C)가 포함된 문장의 본동사는 'call'이며, 뒤에 접속사 없이 컴마가 찍힌 후 뒤의 문장 내용(that절)을 수행하는 상황을 묘사하고 있습니다. 따라서 주절의 주어인 'We(우리)'가 뒤의 행위를 능동적으로 수행하는 분사구문을 써야 하므로, 과거분사인 'hoped'가 아닌 현재분사 'hoping'을 써야 합니다. 정동사와 준동사의 자리를 구분하는 것은 수능 어법의 기본입니다.
keyPoints: (C) 정동사 vs 준동사 — 문장의 본동사 유무 확인 후 분사구문 여부 판정
(A) 전치사 vs 접속사 — 전치사 뒤에 오는 동명사 및 관용 표현 쓰임
(B) 관계대명사 vs 접속사 — 관계대명사 that의 격과 선행사 수식 관계
question.passageWithMarkers: We tend to go long periods of time without __(A) reaching__ out to the people we know. Then, we suddenly take notice of the distance __(B) that__ has formed and we scramble to make repairs. We call people we haven't spoken to in ages, __(C) hoped__ that one small effort will erase the months and years of distance we've created. However, this rarely works: relationships aren't __(D) kept up__ with big one-time fixes. They're kept up with regular maintenance, like a car. In our relationships, we have to make sure that not too much time goes by between oil changes, so to speak. This isn't to say that you __(E) shouldn't bother__ calling someone just because it's been a while since you've spoken; just that it's more ideal not to let yourself fall out of touch in the first place. Consistency always brings better results.

passageText: We tend to go long periods of time without reaching out to the people we know. Then, we suddenly take notice of the distance that has formed and we scramble to make repairs. We call people we haven't spoken to in ages, hoping that one small effort will erase the months and years of distance we've created. However, this rarely works: relationships aren't kept up with big one-time fixes. They're kept up with regular maintenance, like a car. In our relationships, we have to make sure that not too much time goes by between oil changes, so to speak. This isn't to say that you shouldn't bother calling someone just because it's been a while since you've spoken; just that it's more ideal not to let yourself fall out of touch in the first place. Consistency always brings better results.
